Triage first-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_01JEhkB6ShK2HHDzozy7Qwgz`): **promoted to `pm:queue`** · `domain:cli` confirmed (fix lands in `packages/rest`) · type Task (typing hardening; both call sites send valid requests today, no declared contract is violated).

Premises verified on `origin/main` @ `07bfd31cb`: the local structural type sits at `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts:236-248` (`getMetaItems?(req: { type: string }): Promise<{ items: any[] }>` at `:237`, `deletePackage?` at `:241`; call sites `:486`/`:555` with feature-detection guards at `:484`/`:553`). The spec's real shapes exist: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:228` (`GetMetaItemsRequestSchema`), `:2119`, and `getMetaItems` as a required `MetadataProtocol` member at `:2369`. One body correction: the spec file is `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, not under `kernel/` — content claim holds.

The judgement call the body flags (keep optionality vs adopt `MetadataProtocol` whole) is settled by in-flight precedent, not escalation: open draft PR #9845 (#9805, `rest-server.ts`) establishes the exact pattern — request/response types sourced from the spec, optional call + runtime-shaped result handling deliberately preserved. Apply the same here: `getMetaItems?(req: GetMetaItemsRequest): Promise<GetMetaItemsResponse>` etc., keeping the feature-detection. Soft ordering: land after #9845 so the PR can cite the settled convention; no file collision (this card is `package-routes.ts` only — verified against #9845's file list). Clause-②: no — no accept/reject behavior changes; consumer-side typing only. Size/model suggestion: S, opus.

## ⚠️ The card's premise is half false — measure before you follow it

The body says *"Both verbs are already declared in `packages/spec`"*. Measured on `origin/main` @ `301bf26be1`:

- `getMetaItems` ✅ — `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`: `GetMetaItemsRequest` at `:2119`, `GetMetaItemsResponse` at `:2120`, required `MetadataProtocol` member at `:2369`.
- `deletePackage` ⛔ — **grep for `deletePackage`, `DeletePackageRequest`, `DeletePackageResponse` in that file returns ZERO.** There is no declared spec shape to read for this verb.

Triage's comment verified only the `getMetaItems` half (its three cited line numbers are all `getMetaItems`), so this half went unchecked by both of us until now.

⇒ **The deliverable is the `getMetaItems` half.** ⛔ **Do NOT invent a spec declaration for `deletePackage`** — `packages/spec` belongs exclusively to the `domain:spec` seat, and declaring a new protocol verb is a contract act, not a typing cleanup. If you judge `deletePackage` should be declared, **file a card and say so in the report**; leave its local structural type exactly as it is. If measurement shows it *is* declared somewhere I did not look, say where and I will re-scope.

## Scope — the settled convention, applied

Source the request/response types from the spec while **keeping the optionality and the runtime feature-detection**:

```
getMetaItems?(req: GetMetaItemsRequest): Promise< GetMetaItemsResponse >;
```

This is #9805's landed pattern (`45862a53d8`): declared types named, optional call `?.` / `typeof … === 'function'` guards / defensive result reads **deliberately preserved**. `MetadataProtocol` declares `getMetaItems` as **required**; this option is optional and feature-detected at `:484`/`:553`. ⛔ Do not adopt `MetadataProtocol` whole — that changes what the seam tolerates, which is a behaviour question this card does not get to answer.

Locations on `301bf26be1` (⚠️ verify by text, not by number): interface `:227`, `getMetaItems?` `:237`, `deletePackage?` `:241`, guards `:484`/`:553`, call sites `:486`/`:555` (both pass exactly `{ type: 'package' }`), `deletePackage` use `:601`/`:615`.

## Mechanism notes I measured for you — falsifying any of these is a good run

- **Import path**: `@objectstack/spec/api` (that is where `rest-server.ts` reads `GetMetaItemsRequest` from, its line `:71` block). `@objectstack/spec` is **already a `dependencies` entry** of `packages/rest` — no package.json edit should be needed. If one is, stop and say why.
- ⛔ **`TransportScopedMetaRequest` is NOT yours to reuse.** It is a **local, non-exported** alias declared at `rest-server.ts:160`. Both call sites here pass no `environmentId`, so **plain `GetMetaItemsRequest` is the correct type** — you do not need the transport-scoped wrapper. Do not export or hoist that alias: it would drag `rest-server.ts` (the hottest file in this package) into an S-sized card for nothing.
- The response read is `result?.items` at both sites. `GetMetaItemsResponse` also carries `type`; the local shape names only `items`. Naming the declared response may make the optional-chain look redundant to the compiler — **keep the defensive read anyway** (#9805's precedent) and report if the compiler now objects to it.

## Pin

The point of this card is that the spec can move underneath the seam and this module keeps compiling green. ⭐ A test that only asserts today's call sites still work would not notice that. Pin the **coupling**: that the option's request/response types are the spec's, such that a change in `GetMetaItemsRequest` is felt here. A type-level pin (a compile-time assignability assertion) is legitimate evidence here — say plainly which mechanism you chose and what it would catch.

## Closing — the actionable half landed; the other half is **not this lane's**, and it is tracked

PR #9959 merged as `6a12e5efcf`, deliberately marked **`Part of #9846`, not `Fixes`** — the honest marker, because this card's title names **two** verbs and only one was finishable.

### What landed

`PackageRoutesOptions.protocol.getMetaItems` now reads `GetMetaItemsRequest` / `GetMetaItemsResponse` from `@objectstack/spec/api`, with the member kept optional and both call sites' feature-detection preserved (#9805's landed convention). A compile-time exact-type-equality pin holds the coupling — placed in **compiled source** rather than a test file, because this package's `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts` and a type-level assertion there would be compiled by nothing.

### Why `deletePackage` was not done, and will not be done here

This card's premise was **half false**, and measuring it is what settled the scope. The body asserts *"Both verbs are already declared in `packages/spec`"*. Measured — first by me on `protocol.zod.ts`, then more strongly by the implementer across the **whole repo**:

- `getMetaItems` ✅ declared (`GetMetaItemsRequest` `:2119`, `GetMetaItemsResponse` `:2120`, required `MetadataProtocol` member `:2369`)
- `deletePackage` ⛔ **`DeletePackageRequest` / `DeletePackageResponse` return ZERO repo-wide**

There is no declared shape to read. Minting one is a **contract act**, and `packages/spec` belongs exclusively to the `domain:spec` seat — so the remaining half is not work this lane can do, at any priority.

### The residue is tracked, and it is bigger than a typing cleanup

Filed as **#9960**: the three hand-rolled `deletePackage` types **disagree with each other** —

- the implementation (`metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:15379`) names `organizationId` + `keepData`
- the REST option (`package-routes.ts:256`) names neither
- the runtime dispatcher twin (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:895`) reaches the verb through `(protocol as any)` and **routinely sends exactly those two keys** the REST option's type cannot express

No live defect today — the REST registrar only ever sends `{ packageId, allTenants: true }` — and that is correctly not asserted as one. But `organizationId` is the key that decides an uninstall's **blast radius** under `TENANT_SCOPE_REQUIRED`, which makes this worth a card of its own rather than a footnote on a typing card.

### Disposition

Closing as **completed**: everything this card asked for that this lane may do has landed, and keeping it open would mean holding a `domain:cli` card whose only remaining work is a `domain:spec` contract decision already recorded in #9960. If the spec seat declares the verb, the mechanical follow-up here is a fresh card citing #9960, not a re-open of this one.
